content:
Hundreds of flights were cancelled across the northeastern United States due to a technical failure at a major regional air traffic control centre serving the New York City area. Every major airport in New York City ground to a halt for several hours on Monday, as multiple foreign heads of state flew into the country for the United Nations General Assembly.

President Trump's flight from Washington to New York, however, departed on schedule.

The technical failure occurred at a Federal Aviation Administration facility in Philadelphia — the same one that caused repeated flight disruptions at Newark Liberty International Airport in the spring of 2025.

These kinds of regional control centres have two data transmission lines: a primary and a backup. The FAA said a circuit on the primary line failed on Monday morning, and when the system tried to switch to the backup, workers discovered the fibre-optic line had been cut. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy pointed to a construction crew working for Amtrak.

The outage affected flights at airports including Philadelphia, Kennedy, LaGuardia and Newark.

By early afternoon, some flights were resuming at LaGuardia, Kennedy and Philadelphia, but significant delays were still expected throughout the day.

Some airlines were allowing passengers to rebook their flights for free. The FAA advised travellers to check with their airline for flight status before going to the airport.

FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford told reporters the agency was working to restore the primary line as quickly as possible, including installing a new circuit on the primary line, while also working to repair the backup fibre line. He said he could not say how long it would take. Verizon said its technicians were working to restore service as quickly as possible.

"The fibre break is probably a 13-hour fix. It's a massive undertaking," Bedford said in a video interview posted online by a CBS transportation reporter. He said the FAA might be able to install a new circuit to get the primary line working again before the fibre line is repaired.

The primary circuit that failed had been scheduled for replacement as part of a nationwide overhaul of the air traffic control system.

Also on Monday, the FAA began testing a new computer system using artificial intelligence to help predict flight-scheduling conflicts and weather issues, and help air traffic controllers reroute aircraft. But that system is only in early testing in the Washington, D.C., area and does not appear to be related to the ground stop.
